title: Solving System of Linear Equations using Matrix Method
bypass: Step 1: Write system as AX = B where A is coefficient matrix, X is [x,y,z], B is constant column matrix. Step 2: Calculate determinant |A|. If non-zero, calculate adj(A). Step 3: Compute A inverse = adj(A)/|A| and find solution X = (A inverse) * B.

title: Shortest Distance Between Skew Lines
bypass: Use formula: d = |(a2 - a1) dot (b1 cross b2)| / |b1 cross b2|. Step 1: Extract vectors a1, a2, b1, b2. Step 2: Find cross product b1 cross b2 using determinant. Step 3: Find dot product of (a2 - a1) with (b1 cross b2) and divide by magnitude of (b1 cross b2).
graph_visuals: Two non-intersecting non-parallel lines in 3D space with a perpendicular line segment PQ joining them.

title: Bayes' Theorem Applications
triggers: given that the item is defective
what is the probability that it was produced by
bypass: Step 1: Identify partition events E1, E2, E3 (e.g. choice of machine/group) such that sum of P(Ei) = 1. Step 2: Identify result event A (e.g. defective, disease). Step 3: Apply formula P(Ei|A) = [P(Ei) * P(A|Ei)] / sum[P(Ek) * P(A|Ek)].
graph_visuals: Tree diagram representing partition events E1, E2, E3 branching into condition event A and A-bar with corresponding probabilities.

title: Bounded Feasible Region Optimization in LPP
bypass: Step 1: Plot inequality boundary lines on 2D plane and shade the common bounded feasible region. Step 2: Find coordinates of all corner points (intersections). Step 3: Evaluate objective function Z = ax + by at each corner point to identify maximum or minimum value.
graph_visuals: Draw LPP feasible region bounded by constraint lines in the first quadrant with marked corner points A, B, C, D.

title: Area Bounded by Curves using Integration
triggers: area of the region enclosed by
bypass: Step 1: Solve curve equations simultaneously to find point(s) of intersection. Step 2: Set up integral: Area = integral of (y_upper - y_lower) dx or integral of x dy between lower and upper limits. Step 3: Evaluate integral using standard formulas like integral sqrt(a^2 - x^2) dx.
graph_visuals: Draw intersection of curve (e.g. parabola y^2 = 4x or circle x^2 + y^2 = r^2) and straight line, shade the bounded region.

title: Homogeneous Differential Equations
bypass: Step 1: Check dy/dx = F(y/x). Substitute y = v*x, so dy/dx = v + x*(dv/dx). Step 2: Separate variables v and x. Step 3: Integrate both sides, then replace v with (y/x) to get general solution.

title: First-Order Linear Differential Equations
bypass: Step 1: Identify P and Q as functions of x. Step 2: Compute Integrating Factor IF = e^(integral P dx). Step 3: Write solution as y * IF = integral (Q * IF) dx + C and apply initial conditions if particular solution is required.

title: Properties of Definite Integrals (King's Property)
triggers: Evaluate integral from a to b of f(x) dx
bypass: Apply King's Property: I = integral from a to b of f(x) dx = integral from a to b of f(a + b - x) dx. Add the original integral I and converted integral I together (2I) to simplify terms like sin x and cos x or cancel terms in numerator/denominator.

title: Integration of Exponential Special Form e^x [f(x) + f'(x)]
bypass: Break integrand g(x) into two parts f(x) and f'(x) such that integrand becomes e^x * [f(x) + f'(x)]. Direct formula bailout: Result is e^x * f(x) + C.

title: Maxima and Minima Word Problems and Case Studies
bypass: Step 1: Express target variable (Profit, Area, Volume) as single-variable function f(x). Step 2: Solve f'(x) = 0 for critical points x. Step 3: Evaluate f''(x). If f''(x) < 0, x gives maximum; if f''(x) > 0, x gives minimum.
graph_visuals: Graph of polynomial/quadratic profit function showing vertex as maximum point.

title: Continuity of a Piecewise Function at a Point
bypass: For continuity at x = c: Left Hand Limit = Right Hand Limit = f(c). Step 1: Find LHL = limit x->c- f(x). Step 2: Find RHL = limit x->c+ f(x). Step 3: Equate LHL = RHL = f(c) to solve directly for unknown k.
graph_visuals: Piecewise continuous curve meeting smoothly at point x = c without breaks.

title: Adjoint and Determinant Algebraic Properties
bypass: Core Formulas: 1) |adj A| = |A|^(n-1). 2) A * (adj A) = |A| * I. 3) |k A| = k^n * |A|. 4) |A inverse| = 1 / |A|.

title: Proving Equivalence Relations
triggers: a - b is divisible by k
bypass: Must prove 3 conditions: 1) Reflexive: Show (a,a) belongs to R for all a. 2) Symmetric: Assume (a,b) belongs to R and prove (b,a) belongs to R. 3) Transitive: Assume (a,b) and (b,c) belong to R and prove (a,c) belongs to R.

title: Vector Projection and Perpendicular Vectors
triggers: projection of vector a on vector b
bypass: 1) Projection of vector a on vector b = (a dot b) / |b|. 2) Two non-zero vectors a and b are perpendicular/orthogonal if and only if a dot b = 0.
graph_visuals: Right-angled vector triangle showing projection of vector a along line of vector b.

title: Foot of Perpendicular and Image of a Point in 3D
triggers: image of point with respect to line/plane
distance from line parallel to z-axis
bypass: Step 1: Write parametric coordinates of general point L on line in terms of parameter lambda. Step 2: Find direction ratios of PL (where P is given point) and set (direction ratios of PL) dot (direction ratios of line) = 0 to solve for lambda. Step 3: L is foot of perpendicular; Image Q is given by midpoint formula L = (P + Q)/2.
graph_visuals: Diagram showing point P, perpendicular line segment dropping to line/plane at foot L, and extended to image point Q.

title: Intervals of Increasing and Decreasing Functions
bypass: Step 1: Compute first derivative f'(x). Step 2: Find critical numbers where f'(x) = 0. Step 3: Use number line sign test. Function is strictly increasing where f'(x) > 0 and strictly decreasing where f'(x) < 0.
graph_visuals: Number line sign chart indicating positive and negative regions of f'(x).

title: Rate of Change of Quantities
triggers: volume decreases at rate directly proportional to surface area
bypass: Step 1: Write formula relating variables (e.g. Volume V = 4/3 * pi * r^3, Surface Area S = 4 * pi * r^2). Step 2: Differentiate with respect to time t: dV/dt = 4 * pi * r^2 * (dr/dt). Step 3: Substitute given proportionalities to solve for dr/dt.

title: Checking One-One (Injective) and Onto (Surjective) Functions
bypass: 1) One-One: Set f(x1) = f(x2) and simplify algebraically to prove x1 = x2. 2) Onto: Express x in terms of y (x = g(y)) and verify if x belongs to domain for every y in codomain.

title: Integration using Partial Fractions
bypass: Step 1: Decompose integrand P(x)/Q(x) into A/(x-a) + B/(x-b) + ... Step 2: Multiply by denominator and compare coefficients or plug roots of linear factors to find A, B. Step 3: Integrate each log term: integral A/(x-a) dx = A * log|x-a|.

title: Principal Value Branch and Domain of Inverse Trig Functions
triggers: principal value branch of sin^-1 x
bypass: Core Rules: 1) Domain of sin^-1(g(x)) or cos^-1(g(x)) is -1 <= g(x) <= 1. 2) Range (Principal Value Branch) of sin^-1 x is [-pi/2, pi/2], cos^-1 x is [0, pi], tan^-1 x is (-pi/2, pi/2).

title: Area of Parallelogram and Triangle Using Vectors
triggers: area of parallelogram formed by adjacent sides
bypass: 1) Area of Parallelogram with adjacent side vectors a and b = |a cross b|. 2) Area of Triangle with adjacent side vectors a and b = 0.5 * |a cross b|. Use determinant method for cross product.
graph_visuals: Parallelogram OACB formed by adjacent vectors a (OA) and b (OB).

title: Order and Degree of Differential Equations
bypass: Order = Highest derivative present in the equation. Degree = Power of the highest derivative after polynomializing the equation (freeing derivatives from radicals/fractions). Degree is undefined if derivatives are inside trigonometric or log functions.

title: Unbounded Feasible Region LPP Optimization
triggers: open half plane has points in common
bypass: Step 1: Identify corner points of unbounded region and calculate objective value Z at each. Let M be candidate minimum. Step 2: Graph open half-plane ax + by < M. Step 3: If open half-plane shares NO common points with feasible region, M is minimum. If it shares common points, Z has NO minimum value.
graph_visuals: Unbounded feasible region shaded outwards with open dashed boundary line ax + by < M crossing the graph.

title: Independent Events and Probability Operations
triggers: probability of selection of at least one
bypass: Core Formulas for Independent Events A and B: 1) P(A intersection B) = P(A) * P(B). 2) P(exactly one occurs) = P(A)P(B') + P(B)P(A'). 3) P(at least one occurs) = 1 - P(A') * P(B').
graph_visuals: Venn diagram representing independent events A and B with intersecting and complement regions.

title: Logarithmic Differentiation for Variable Powers
bypass: Step 1: Take natural logarithm on both sides: log y = v * log u. Step 2: Differentiate implicitly with respect to x: (1/y) * dy/dx = v' * log u + v * (u'/u). Step 3: Multiply by y to isolate dy/dx and substitute y = u^v.
